note: Nothing on this list blocks publication. Each row states what was found, why it matters, and what would clear it. Severity: BLOCKING means it blocks a specific claim (named in the row), not the site.

flags.item: No official NFL source publishes betting lines, and no 2026 closing or prop prices exist anywhere in this repository.
flags.detail: The league publishes results, stats and injury reports. Prices live with licensed operators. The only prices in the repo are a third-party 1999-2026 closing-line archive inside the peer nfl-quant workspace. Consequence: every 2026 market, divergence, edge and ROI cell on this site is blank.
flags.action: Obtain a licensed price archive with timestamps before any 2026 price comparison is published.

flags.item: No authorised player-level game logs and no prop prices, so player-prop strategies and prop correlations cannot be graded.
flags.detail: nfl.com publishes season-to-date player leaderboards only. A peer workspace graded props against a rolling-mean proxy line and its own flags record that the gate fails by construction. Those numbers are not imported here; the corresponding cells are blank.
flags.action: Licensed player-game data plus archived prop prices; then re-register the gate.

flags.item: The starter/backup question cannot be answered from official sources: nfl.com has no depth chart and no snap counts.
flags.detail: https://www.nfl.com/teams/washington-commanders/depth-chart/ returns a 404 (checked 2026-11-12). Club roster pages give position, number, height, weight, experience and college only. The injury page gives practice and game status only. No row on this site asserts that a player is a 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacement.
flags.action: A licensed depth chart with snap counts, or club-issued depth charts captured weekly.

flags.item: The 1.5-point home-field value used for the 2026 originated lines is a model assumption, not an official value.
flags.detail: Home-field advantage is not published by the NFL. Our walk-forward historical estimate exists, but a 2026-only estimate cannot be separated from it with 9 games per club. The number is disclosed on the own-lines page next to every line it produced.
flags.action: Either publish a measured HFA with a confidence interval or keep the label. Do not present it as official.

flags.item: Our model is less accurate than the closing line: spread MAE 10.502 vs 9.871 points; total 10.830 vs 10.470.
flags.detail: This is a negative result and it is the headline. It also means gate G4 fails for every strategy, so no strategy can be Qualified in this release. Presenting any of the originated lines as an edge would contradict the repository's own numbers.
flags.action: None: publish as-is. Revisit only with a pre-registered model change.

flags.item: The model's 90% interval covers 89.34% of holdout games (fine) but the mean residual is +0.651 points (fails the pre-registered 0.5 bar).
flags.detail: The interval width is right and the centre is skewed toward the away team by about two-thirds of a point. Gate G3 therefore fails on the bias test only.
flags.action: A pre-registered v1.1 with a corrected home-field term; must be a new gate version, not a tweak after the fact.

flags.item: The peer 2026 game archive in nfl-lab/data/games_2026.csv was missing 16 of 136 games (all of Week 9 plus the Week 8 Monday game).
flags.detail: The file held 120 rows. Using it as-is would have understated every club's games played by one or two and corrupted any rate statistic. The 16 missing games were read from the official week pages and added in nfl-edge/data/games_2026.json (peer file left untouched); the combined archive now reconciles to the official standings with 0 mismatches.
flags.action: The owning session should either adopt nfl-edge/data/games_2026.json or refresh its own generator to include weeks 8-9.

flags.item: The peer archive nfl-quant/data/predictions.csv contains 272 rows tagged season 2026, but the 2026 season is only at Week 10 (136 games played).
flags.detail: Rows for unplayed games may be fixtures, placeholders or mislabelled seasons. This session used that file only for 1999-2025 completed games with a recorded result, so no 2026 row affected any result published here. The inconsistency itself is unverified and is left for its owning session.
flags.action: Owning session to confirm what the 2026 rows represent.

flags.item: Two datasets are corroborated by aggregate identity rather than by re-reading every page.
flags.detail: 120 of the 136 game scores come from a peer archive whose rows carry the official game-page URL; they are accepted because the aggregate W-L-T and PF-PA over all 136 games reproduces the official standings exactly for all 32 clubs. That is strong but not identical to reading every game page. The 16 restored games were read directly.
flags.action: Optional: spot-check the 120 inherited scores against the official game pages before any high-stakes use.

flags.item: The official team-statistics pages are HTML tables with no stable machine-readable export; every value on this site was transcribed by hand into JSON.
flags.detail: Transcription was defended with six league-wide identities (offence equals defence across the league for pass yards, pass TDs, rush yards, rush TDs, points and points against: 63,556 / 411 / 30,580 / 257 / 6,246 / 6,246). A single transposed digit inside a team row would not be caught by that test.
flags.action: Add a second independent read per row (suggestion S-16).

flags.item: Gate thresholds (300 bets, 60% positive seasons, |bias| < 0.5, p < 0.05) are research design choices, not official NFL values.
flags.detail: They are labelled as design choices and frozen in a versioned file before the backtest ran. They should be reviewed by a statistician before any reward is paid against them.
flags.action: Independent review of gate thresholds (suggestion S-05).

flags.item: The repository carries 53 MB of raw archived HTML/JSON in data/raw/, four tracked .pyc files, and about twenty parallel workspaces including three competing SF rental sites.
flags.detail: Only the first two are objectively wrong: .pyc files are build artefacts and data/raw/ is a scrape dump. The workspace duplication is a discoverability problem with a correctness risk, because two dashboards can disagree while both claim to be verified.
flags.action: Add data/raw/ and __pycache__/ to .gitignore; untrack .pyc; decide on one canonical dashboard (suggestions S-11).

flags.item: The repository root index.html is generated by verification/build.py and running it deletes any hand-added navigation link.
flags.detail: This session confirmed it: regenerating the site in a scratch copy drops the 'LOCAL ADDITION' rental links and mine. That is why this session appended its link additively and did not run the root generator. The root page belongs to the NBA final-integration session.
flags.action: Add the NFL link to verification/build.py NAV and regenerate, or accept that the NFL page is reachable by URL only from the root.

flags.item: The injury dataset is a single snapshot taken 2026-11-12; the official report moves daily and game status is final only 90 minutes before kickoff.
flags.detail: Every availability row is timestamped and should be re-read before being used for anything. No automated daily capture exists yet (suggestion S-09).

flags.item: A negative holdout ROI does not prove the model is worthless, and a positive one would not prove skill.
flags.detail: The strategies here are simple, publicly computable rules tested against efficient closing lines. The expected outcome is approximately -vig, which is what was found. The leaderboard is a rejection machine, and it rejected everything; that is the design working, not a bug.
flags.action: Read the leaderboard as 'what survived', not 'what lost'.

flags.item: No jurisdiction, licence or terms-of-use decision exists for this project.
flags.detail: Data here is transcribed from the league's public pages for research. Redistribution, commercial use and any real-money activity would need terms review and local legal advice; none has been obtained.
flags.action: Answer Q12 before any commercial use.
